data.narrative:
Asimov, a Series B-stage biotech company founded by Chris Voigt, Doug Densmore, Alec Nielsen, and Raja Srinivas, has raised $209M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable set spanning 3 public equities (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, including Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), New Limit ($3.1B), and Eikon Therapeutics ($539M).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression, using total raised as a proxy base, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying a valuation of $397M. Peer-median valuation across the 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields $3.5B, with a range spanning $539M to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (median 6.6x across the sector) cannot be applied, as Asimov's revenue is not disclosed. Revenue-based methods remain inaccessible for private-company analysis without public disclosure.

The two applicable methods produce a wide range. The triangulated analysis supports a valuation band of $338M (low) to $4.0B (high), with a median of $1.9B. This dispersion reflects tension between stage-derived estimates anchored to capital raised and peer multiples skewed by later-stage, high-valuation outliers. Key uncertainties include Asimov's revenue trajectory, burn rate, and competitive positioning relative to the peer set, particularly the $10.3B outlier.
